newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's opposition group sends envoys to Kabila.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's opposition group sends envoys to Kabila.

text.p: Zaire's main opposition group said on Thursday that it had sent envoys to talk to rebel leader Laurent Kabila.

"We have delegates en route to meet Mr Kabila," Adrien Phongo, general-secretary of the radical Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS), told a news conference, adding that informal contacts had already been made.

The UDPS of veteran radical Etienne Tshisekedi, a long-standing opponent of ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko, is doing its utmost to unseat Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo, who returned to Kinshasa on Thursday saying the job was still his.
Citing a disputed Tuesday vote in Zaire's transitional parliament to sack Kengo, Phongo urged Mobutu to endorse Tshisekedi as Zaire's new prime minister.

A national conference elected Tshisekedi prime minister in 1992 but Mobutu sacked him a year later in favour of one of his own appointees. Tshisekedi has never accepted Kengo's appointment in 1994 as a compromise candidate.

Mobutu, who left hospital in Europe on Wednesday, plans to return to Zaire on Friday to seek a political solution to Zaire's deepening crisis, according to his son. The rebels insist on face-to-face talks with Mobutu before any ceasefire.
